prompt:
You are a senior engineer on the Rust compiler team. The core team is evaluating PR #132833, which proposes stabilizing let chains in the 2024 edition. Before this stabilization can proceed, the language design group has requested a written Design Document that distills the stabilization rationale, the technical constraints, and the implementation impact into a structured reference for cross-team review.

Materials provided:
- The full PR #132833 diff and stabilization report (attached as `pr_132833_stabilization_report.md`)
- The tracking issue reference: rust-lang/rust#53667
- The RFC reference: rust-lang/rfcs#2497

Task requirements:
1. Create a Markdown design document titled exactly `Design Doc - Let Chains Stabilization in Rust 2024`.
2. Include the following sections in order, each with the specified heading:
   - **Executive Summary**: A one-paragraph overview of what is being stabilized and why it is edition-bound.
   - **Feature Description**: Explain the syntax being stabilized (chaining `let` with `&&` in `if`/`while`), including a brief code example. Reference RFC 2497.
   - **Edition Justification**: Explain why this feature is restricted to the 2024 edition, specifically addressing the drop order changes and MIR generation issues. Reference tracking issue #53667 and the drop order changes issue #124085.
   - **Implementation Details**: Describe the key changes in the parser, focusing on the introduction of `LetChainsPolicy::EditionDependent` and the modification to `parse_expr_cond` in `compiler/rustc_parse/src/parser/expr.rs`. Note the removal of the `ungate_last` call.
   - **Transition Plan**: Outline the proposal to keep the `let_chains` feature gate available for a limited time (roughly 3 months) on older editions for nightly users.
   - **Risks and Open Questions**: Identify at least two risks or open questions, such as adoption friction for users on older editions or the timeline for deprecating the feature gate.
   - **References**: List the tracking issue, RFC, and any linked PRs or issues mentioned in the PR description.
3. Use bullet points where appropriate (e.g., in Risks and Open Questions).
4. Include the code example from the PR description in a Rust code block.
5. The document must be self-contained and written in a professional technical tone suitable for a design review meeting.

Deliverable specification:
- Output a single Markdown file.
- Use level-1 heading for the title, level-2 headings for each section.
- Include a Markdown code block with the example `FnCall` struct and its methods.
- Do not include any information not present in the provided materials.

md_sections.heading: Design Doc - Let Chains Stabilization in Rust 2024
required_content: Title matches exactly 'Design Doc - Let Chains Stabilization in Rust 2024'

md_sections.heading: Executive Summary
paragraphs: This document outlines the stabilization plan for the `let_chains` feature (RFC 2497, tracking issue #53667) in the Rust 2024 edition. The feature enables chaining `let` statements with `&&` inside `if` and `while` expressions, allowing intermixture with boolean expressions. Stabilization is restricted to the 2024 edition due to critical drop order changes required for correct MIR generation, ensuring consistency between `if let` and `if let` chains. This design document summarizes the rationale, implementation changes, transition plan, and open risks.

md_sections.heading: Feature Description
Edition Justification
required_content: Reference to drop order changes issue #124085
paragraphs:
The restriction to the 2024 edition is driven by drop order inconsistencies and MIR generation challenges. In older editions, the drop order of temporaries in `if let` chains differs from that of a simple `if let`. As noted in the stabilization report, "If we want `if let` chains to be compatible with `if let`, drop order makes it hard for us to [generate correct MIR]. It would be strange to have different behaviour for `if let ... {}` and `if true && let ... {}`."

Edition 2024 introduced [drop order changes](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/124085) that make temporaries in `if let` live more shortly, resolving the inconsistency. These changes are necessary for correct function of let chains, not merely a behavioral improvement. Therefore, stabilizing the feature on older editions would either break existing code or produce incorrect MIR.

The specific MIR generation problem is documented in [issue #104843](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/104843). The decision to tie the feature to the edition was discussed in [PR #103293 comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/103293#issuecomment-1293408574).

md_sections.heading: Implementation Details
paragraphs:
The implementation modifies the parser in `compiler/rustc_parse/src/parser/expr.rs` to enforce edition-dependent let chain behavior.

Key changes include:
- Introduction of the `LetChainsPolicy::EditionDependent` variant, which carries the current edition from the span of the `if` or `while` expression.
- Modification of `parse_expr_cond` to accept a `LetChainsPolicy` parameter instead of no arguments. The method signature changed from `pub fn parse_expr_cond(&mut self) -> PResult<'a, P<Expr>>` to `pub fn parse_expr_cond(&mut self, let_chains_policy: LetChainsPolicy) -> PResult<'a, P<Expr>>`.
- The `CondChecker` is now initialized with the policy: `CondChecker::new(self, let_chains_policy)`.
- The call to `self.psess.gated_spans.ungate_last(sym::let_chains, cond.span)` was removed because the feature is now stable in edition 2024.
- In `parse_expr_if`, the policy is set with `LetChainsPolicy::EditionDependent { current_edition: lo.edition() }`, where `lo` is the span of the `if` token. A similar change is made in `parse_expr_while`.
- The PR adds `use rustc_span::edition::Edition;` to the imports.

md_sections.heading: Transition Plan
required_content: Limited feature gate availability on older editions
paragraphs:
To ease adoption, the `let_chains` feature gate will remain available for nightly users on older editions for a limited time after stabilization. The stabilization report proposes "to continue offering the `let_chains` feature (behind a feature gate) for a limited time (maybe 3 months after stabilization?) on older editions to allow nightly users to adopt edition changes."

This allows projects not yet on edition 2024 to test and migrate incrementally without losing access to let chains. After the transition period, the feature gate will be removed for pre-2024 editions, and the error message will direct users to update their edition.

md_sections.heading: Risks and Open Questions
required_content: At least two risks or open questions
paragraphs:
- **Adoption friction**: Users on older editions will not have access to let chains without a feature gate. This may slow adoption and create confusion, especially for large projects with multi-edition codebases.
- **Feature gate deprecation timeline**: The proposed 3-month window is informal; a concrete decision on the exact duration and communication plan is needed.
- **Compatibility with future editions**: While the feature is stabilized for 2024 and beyond, future edition changes to drop order or pattern matching must be coordinated to avoid regressions.
- **Documentation gaps**: The stabilization report links to several issues and PRs, but comprehensive user-facing documentation for the new syntax and edition restrictions may be required.

md_sections.heading: References
paragraphs:
- [Tracking Issue #53667](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/53667)
- [RFC 2497](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2497)
- [Drop Order Changes Issue #124085](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/124085)
- [MIR Generation Issue #104843](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/104843)
- [PR #103293 Comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/103293#issuecomment-1293408574)
- [2024 Edition Guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/edition-guide/rust-2024/index.html)
